match_note: Nature Communications NCOMMS-25-92789. Same title, claims and numbers as arXiv v1 (300 meV gap, DFT 319 meV, 20-island statistics, WCC Z2=1, HSE06, 10 ps AIMD, edge peak with 2-3 nm extent, lower-edge signal loss). But Fig. 5 differs in detail: referees cite dI/dV maps in Fig. 5(e)-(g) and an edge peak 'a few meV below EF' in Fig. 5b, while v1 Fig. 5 has panels (a)-(e) with a single +7 mV map and the peak described 'at EF'. R1 quotes an 'uninterrupted' contour claim, whereas v1 already concedes minor degradation at the lower edge. So the submitted version is a close variant of v1, not identical. Several concerns target the SI (Figs. S10, S13, p.14), which is not in the v1 PDF but is cited from it as Ref. 35; those are marked in_v1 true. Round 2: all three referees recommend acceptance with no new concerns.

concerns.quote: edge-enhanced LDOS alone is not unique to QSH systems. Trivial edge resonances, band bending, or reconstruction-induced states can mimic similar phenomenology.
concerns.summary: The in-gap edge peak could come from trivial edge resonances, band bending, reconstruction states, bulk states near EF or substrate-induced interface states rather than topological edge modes.
concerns.note: R3 adds bulk states near EF and substrate interface states. Authors concede STM/STS cannot exclude all trivial states; added nanoribbon charge-density DFT and argued spatial localization rules out substrate/interface origin.

concerns.quote: The authors should provide additional evidence or a control experiment (beyond edge vs bulk contrast)
concerns.summary: A control experiment or a more direct probe (R3 suggests momentum-resolved ARPES) is needed beyond edge-versus-center contrast to verify the edge-state origin.
concerns.note: Authors cite their earlier Sb2Te3-substrate work (trivial phase, no edge states) as a control; ARPES declined as lacking spatial resolution and out of scope.

concerns.quote: Strong evidence that this edge state is topologically protected by time reversal symmetry is, however, lacking. The authors should mention this explicitly
concerns.summary: Nothing in the data shows the edge state is protected by time-reversal symmetry, and the paper should say so.
concerns.note: Added explicit statement that TRS protection is not established; transport suggested as future work.

concerns.quote: statements describing continuous edge rings as direct spectroscopic confirmation of topological modes should be written in a more cautious and technically rigorous tone.
concerns.summary: Several sentences, including the abstract, are promotional and assert more than the evidence supports.

concerns.quote: The islands are very small, the reported edge-state spatial extent (~2-3 nm) takes a substantial fraction of the island lateral size, coupled with tip-convolution this would obstruct of measuring the true bandgap
concerns.summary: Because islands are small relative to the edge-state width and tip convolution, the measured bulk gap may be unreliable; statistics on larger islands or a size-scaling analysis are needed.
concerns.note: Authors re-presented the existing 20-island, 4-tip statistics (284 +/- 51 meV) from the original SI and argued larger islands are not yet growable; no new larger-island data.

concerns.quote: edge states might hybridize with each other which could open a bandgap in the edge state spectrum.
concerns.summary: In such small islands, opposite edge states could hybridize and gap out the edge spectrum.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Width-dependent nanoribbon DFT showing hybridization suppressed above ~4.59 nm.

concerns.quote: The penetration depth of the edges states is typically inversely proportional to the gap size... I would anticipate... very small spatial extend of the edge states, probably much smaller than the 2-3 nm
concerns.summary: A ~300 meV gap should give edge states much narrower than the 2-3 nm observed, an apparent inconsistency.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: New nanoribbon charge-density DFT (~2 nm) plus comparison to Bi(111) bilayer literature. Note v1 itself quotes DFT ~1.35 nm vs ~2 nm (map) vs 2-3 nm (line spectra).

concerns.quote: The decay length of approximately 2 nm is inferred indirectly from nanoribbon calculations... A more convincing demonstration would involve plotting spatially resolved edge-state wavefunctions
concerns.summary: The DFT decay length is inferred only indirectly from where edge crossings appear in ribbons, rather than from spatially resolved wavefunctions.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Nanoribbon calculations are in the SI, cited from v1 main text (DFT ~1.35 nm).

concerns.quote: I do not agree with the statement by the authors that the edge state runs uninterrupted along the whole contour of the flake in Figure 5, there is an obvious and big interruption
concerns.summary: The dI/dV map shows a large break at the bottom edge, contradicting the claim of a continuous edge ring; more maps are needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: New higher-resolution maps at +5.5 and +8.5 mV; wording softened; suppression attributed to tip effects. v1 text already notes 'minor signal degradation at a small segment of the lower edge'.

concerns.quote: Given the islands appear to have rough edges, the STS signature should vary along different edges/segments or with this roughness.
concerns.summary: Edge terminations and roughness should change the edge-state dispersion, so spectra along different edge segments are needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: New spectra on different edge segments of the Fig. 5d island (Fig. R5).

concerns.quote: the edge-bulk correspondence tells that the boundary state is midgap, however the reported edge states are significantly offset from the midgap.
concerns.summary: The edge-state peak sits far from midgap, which is unexpected for a topological boundary state.

concerns.quote: The gap assignment from Fig. 4 is not fully convincing and may be internally inconsistent, as in Figure 5 b and c there is no clear bandgap.
concerns.summary: The ~300 meV gap from Fig. 4 is not clearly visible in the Fig. 5 spectra, so the gap assignment may be inconsistent.
concerns.note: Attributed to metallic HfTe2 background; cited existing 20-island statistics.

concerns.quote: What causes the dip in the bulk spectrum of SiTe2 in Figure 5, and why there is no bulk bandgap visible in these spectra?
concerns.summary: The origin of the V-shaped dip in the island-center spectrum, and the absence of a visible bulk gap there, is unexplained.

concerns.quote: Can the authors add a clear structural model in the main text?
concerns.summary: A clear structural model should appear in the main text.
concerns.note: Authors noted Fig. 1b,c already show it; added 3D views.

concerns.quote: there are parts where arrows and other marks are not explained in the captions.
concerns.summary: Figure captions leave arrows and other marks unexplained.

concerns.quote: I do not see any evidence for this non-linearity in Figure 2(b) and therefore I suggest another explanation.
concerns.summary: The edge peak (where linear 1D dispersion predicts flat DOS) may come from momentum-dependent tunneling matrix elements rather than an unsupported van Hove singularity; check against the Fermi velocity.
concerns.note: Added discussion of both mechanisms and a Fermi-velocity estimate from Fig. 2b.

concerns.quote: I suggest shifting this discussion (first two paragraphs on page 14 of the supplementary materials section) to the main text.
concerns.summary: The SI discussion of the interior peak near -10 meV should move to the main text.

concerns.quote: Can the authors also show a dI/dV map taken at the peak position of the edge state (a few meV below the Fermi level)?
concerns.summary: dI/dV maps are shown only above EF; a map at the edge-state peak energy is needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Authors clarified spectra and maps came from different islands (peak at +7 mV for the mapped island) and added maps at +5.5 and +8.5 mV.

concerns.quote: The WCC results can strongly depend on several computational parameters... The authors should clarify convergence with respect to these parameters
concerns.summary: The Wannier charge center Z2 calculation lacks methodological detail and convergence checks.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Added Wannier details and Wannier-vs-HSE band comparison (Fig. R8).

concerns.quote: the nanoribbon band structure of Si2Te2 suggests that topological edge states coexist energetically with bulk states
concerns.summary: In the nanoribbon bands (SI Fig. S13) edge states overlap in energy with bulk states at EF, undermining dissipationless transport.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Recomputed ribbons 0.56-8.62 nm; replaced SI Fig. S13. Figure is in the SI, not the v1 PDF.

concerns.quote: phonon-mediated scattering in telluride-based systems is expected to be non-negligible and is not addressed in the manuscript.
concerns.summary: Phonon-mediated scattering, likely significant in tellurides, is not considered.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The authors should discuss the robustness of their conclusions with respect to the choice of exchange-correlation functional.
concerns.summary: Band inversion from HSE may not be robust; GW corrections can change the topological classification in tellurides.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: New GW calculations showing the same SOC-driven inversion at Gamma.

concerns.quote: The presented stability analysis appears limited to short-time simulations, and practical device applicability requires a clearer discussion of environmental robustness.
concerns.summary: Stability under ambient temperature and pressure is not established; the 10 ps AIMD is too short.
concerns.note: 100 ps AIMD added plus UHV/annealing arguments; no ambient (air) exposure data.

first_round.quote: However, the current paper, particularly the QSH claim, requires additional analysis, control experiments, and more internally consistent evidence.
In its present form, I cannot recommend publication. However, after satisfactory revision this manuscript might be suitable for publication in Nature Communications.
Several conceptual and methodological assumptions require stronger justification. The manuscript, in its present form, remains inconclusive regarding the topological nature of the grown samples.

recommendations.note: Only Version 0 (first round) was used. The file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal. No referee co-signed another's report. None of the three used an explicit recommendation term, so each level is inferred. R2 is the closest call. It is called major because the referee says it cannot be published in its present form and asks for a new dI/dV map, although its other requests are mostly discussion changes. R3 was rated major rather than reject because the report asks for stronger justification and extra checks (Wannier convergence, wavefunction plots, GW, ARPES, stability) rather than declaring the paper unsuitable.
recommendations.label: contested
